help.title: How it works
help.intro: You email a note: it becomes a topic and proposed cards. You validate the cards, then review a little every day.

send.title: Send
send.address: Your sending address is {address}. Write from your account address ({accountEmail}), otherwise the message is refused.
send.what: You can send a few words, a link, a PDF or a photo, up to {maxItems} sources per email. A file can weigh up to {maxFileMb} MB, a photo up to {maxPhotoMb} MB.
send.receipt: Proposed cards arrive in the tray, with the list of your received mails at the bottom. If processing fails, an email tells you why and what to do.
send.tryHint: This opens your mail app with a sample note, which you can edit before sending. The cards arrive in the tray within a few minutes.

tray.title: {tray}
tray.keep: Proposed cards wait in "{tray}". Nothing enters your reviews unless you keep it: "{keep}", "{discard}" or "{keepAll}".
tray.badge: The "{badgeModel}" badge means the card comes from the AI's own knowledge, not from your source.

review.title: {review}
review.grades: "{show}", then grade yourself with four buttons: "{again}", "{hard}", "{good}", "{easy}".
review.forgot: If you forgot, always pick "{again}", never "{hard}".
review.budget: Your daily review time is {budget} min (choices: {presets}). When the day is full, new cards wait. Once the time is up, you can choose "{continueAnyway}".
review.edit: "{edit}" fixes the wording of a card; "{suspend}" takes it out of your reviews.

reminder.title: The reminder
reminder.when: A reminder goes out at {reminderTime} on study days, only when there is something to do.
reminder.link: Its link opens the session without signing in for {tokenHours} h. It can only review: no editing, no topics, no "{settings}".
reminder.pause: You can pause or stop the reminder from the email or from "{settings}".

pages.title: {pages} / {settings}
pages.pages: Every send creates or enriches a topic, with its sources; find them in "{pages}".
pages.settings: In "{settings}", you set your review time, your days, how many new cards, the target retention, the time zone, the language, the style, the reminders and your data.

about.title: Why it works
about.lede: {brand} rests on a few research findings about memory, and on a few product choices. This page says which, where they come from, and where the evidence stops.

forgetting.title: Forgetting is normal
forgetting.theory: We forget what we have just learned quickly, then more and more slowly. Researchers call this the forgetting curve. Each time we successfully recall something, it fades more slowly.
forgetting.memento: So each card comes back after an interval that grows each time you recall it.

testing.title: Testing yourself beats rereading
testing.theory: Searching your memory for the answer helps you retain more than rereading the lesson or highlighting. In a review of the literature on ten study techniques, self-testing is among the two techniques rated most useful.
testing.memento: {brand} shows you the question first and lets you answer from memory before revealing the answer.

spacing.title: Spacing out your reviews
spacing.theory: Reviewing in several sittings, with breaks, helps you retain more than going over everything at once. The authors of the same review also place spacing among the two most useful techniques. The ideal gap depends on how long you want to remember: the further away the target date, the more the reviews can be spaced out.
spacing.memento: Each successful answer lengthens the gap before the card's next review.

fsrs.title: How {brand} picks the next date
fsrs.algorithm: {brand} uses a free, public algorithm, FSRS. For each card it tracks three things: its difficulty, the strength of the memory and the probability of remembering it today.
fsrs.memento: When you grade an answer ({again}, {hard}, {good}, {easy}), it recalculates the next date so that your chance of remembering stays close to the level you chose in the settings. The default is {retention}%.

cards.title: Why cards go through you
cards.memento: The AI reads what you send and proposes cards; it adds none to your reviews without your approval. Facts taken from your source quote their excerpt; what the AI adds from its own knowledge is flagged as unverified. This is not a research result.

budget.title: A few minutes, every day
budget.memento: {brand} limits the review time you set per day: when the day is full, new cards wait. This is not a research result: it is so the pace stays sustainable.

about.limits: These results come from laboratory and classroom studies, mostly on word lists and courses; they guarantee nothing for any one person. FSRS is a model of memory, not a measurement of yours. Cards written by an AI can be wrong: reread them before keeping them.
about.helpLink: Why it works: the theory and the sources

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lede: {brand} is in beta, built by one person. Here is what is kept, by whom, and how to erase everything.
privacy.store: The emails you send (text, links, attachments), the text read from links and files, the topics and cards made from them, your review history, your settings and your email address. Nothing else: no advertising, no resale, no tracking.

gemini.name: Google (Gemini API)
gemini.role: reads your content to extract facts and cards, and to compare it with your topics.

supabase.name: Supabase
supabase.role: database and files, hosted in the eu-west-3 region (Paris).

resend.name: Resend
resend.role: sending and receiving email (processing failures, reminders, sign-in codes, waiting-list confirmation).

cloudflare.name: Cloudflare
cloudflare.role: domain name management only; the content of your emails does not go through it.

privacy.noTrain: AI calls use Google's paid offer, whose terms say content is not used to improve its products.
privacy.yourRights: In Settings you can download all your data and delete your account. Deletion is immediate: the account, topics, cards, history and original files are erased. Only cost lines remain, with no content and no identity.
privacy.waitlist: If you leave your address on the home page to be told when it opens, a confirmation email is sent and nothing is stored until you click its button. Once you confirm, only your address, the language of the page and the date of confirmation are kept. The address is used only to send you one email on the day it opens: no other mail, no sharing, no tracking. It is erased at the latest {months} months after you confirmed.
privacy.waitlistRemove: To remove it sooner, use the “{leaveLink}” link in the confirmation email. Lost it? Enter your address again on the home page: the new email has that link too.
privacy.waitlistAbuse: To limit abuse, a fingerprint (hash) of the email address and of the network (IP) address of each request is kept for at most two days.
privacy.contact: For any question, ask the person who invited you.

landing.metaDescription: Email a link, a PDF, a photo or two lines: {brand} turns it into cards and has you review them a little every day. Closed beta.
landing.hook: You email a link, a PDF, a photo or two lines to one address. {brand} turns it into cards worth remembering and has you review them a little every day.

notify.title: Hear when it opens
notify.lede: The beta is closed, by invitation only. Leave your address: once you confirm it, you will get one email, on the day {brand} opens to everyone.
notify.consent: Your address is used only to tell you when it opens. Nothing else, and you can remove it whenever you want. <link>What is kept</link>

status.sent: Almost done: a confirmation email is on its way. Click its button to be on the list. Nothing yet? Check your spam folder.
status.limited: Too many requests right now. Try again later.
status.failed: The email could not be sent. Try again in a moment.

send.title: You send
send.text: Write to your {brand} address from your usual mail app: a few words about a visit, a link to an article, a PDF, a photo of a museum panel. Proposed cards arrive in the tray; if something fails, an email explains it.

sort.title: You validate
sort.text: {brand} files what you send into topics by subject and proposes a few question-and-answer cards. You keep the ones worth it and drop the rest.

review.title: You review
review.text: A few minutes a day, cards come back when it is time to see them again. You say whether you remembered, and the schedule adjusts.

diff.title: What is different
diff.choose: You choose what enters your reviews: no card gets there without your say.
diff.sources: Every fact cites its source. Anything the AI adds from its own knowledge is marked as such.
diff.reminder: One email reminder at the time you choose, only on days when there is something to do.
diff.budget: A daily review time you set: when the day is full, new cards wait.

beta.title: A beta, built by one person
beta.text: {brand} is in closed beta, built by one person. No advertising, no resale, no tracking. Things will still change.

reason.too_short: It is too short for me to get anything out of it. Add a few sentences, or forward the article itself.
reason.no_claims: I could not extract reliable facts from it. Try pasting the text directly into the email.
reason.fetch_error: I could not read the content of the email. Send it again in a few minutes.
reason.ai_error: My analysis failed after several tries. Send the note again in a few minutes.
reason.unknown: An unexpected error occurred. Send the note again in a few minutes.
reason.paywall: The page is for subscribers only or asks you to sign in. Copy the article's text into a new email.
reason.empty_page: I found almost no text on that page (it may load through scripts). Copy the article's text into a new email.
reason.url_blocked: I cannot open this link (address not allowed). Copy the page's text into a new email.
reason.page_error: The page could not be loaded (it no longer exists or refuses access). Check the link or copy the text into a new email.
reason.unsupported_link: This link does not lead to a readable web page (a file or document). Send the file as an attachment.
reason.file_too_large: The file is too large (25 MB maximum, 15 MB for a scanned document or an image). Send a lighter version.
reason.unsupported_file: I only read PDFs and images (photos, screenshots). Send the content in one of those formats or paste the text into the email.
reason.unreadable_file: I could not read anything in this file (password-protected, damaged or empty). Try another version or paste the text into the email.
